turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I’m here because I spend most of the day checking things around the house—outlets, locks, tools, even dust—and fixing or rechecking them over and over. I get worn out, but I still don’t feel sure enough to just leave it alone.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient reports repetitive checking and rechecking of outlets, locks, tools, and dust-related concerns despite exhaustion and inability to feel sufficiently reassured.

turns.doctor_question: What specific thought or fear goes through your mind if you try to stop yourself from checking?
turns.patient_response: Even if I know I did it right, I get these thoughts that I missed a loose wire and the house is going to burn down, or that I left a nail somewhere and my wife will get hurt. I try to tell myself it’s done, but the thoughts just come back stronger.

symptom_reasoning.S065: He describes recurrent unwanted fears that he missed a loose wire or nail, causing harm, which return more strongly when he tries to dismiss them.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been dealing with these thoughts and repetitive checking behaviors?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure how long exactly. It’s been going on for a while, but I can’t pin down when it started.

turns.doctor_question: How has this checking routine affected your ability to manage your daily responsibilities?
turns.patient_response: It’s affected things a lot. I stopped taking paid carpentry jobs because I can’t get out of the house without getting stuck checking everything. I’ve also pulled back from the community projects I used to help with. My wife does more of the errands and makes more of the decisions now, because I get caught up in it and end up exhausted.

symptom_reasoning.S066: He describes becoming stuck checking everything before leaving the house, consistent with repetitive checking behavior.
